cc-madhya-3.170.translation: Śacīmātā submitted, "As far as you are concerned, you can meet Nimāi, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, many times somewhere else, but what is the possibility of my ever meeting Him again? I shall have to remain at home. A sannyāsī never returns to his home."

lines: muñi bhikṣā dimu, sabākāre māgoṅ dāna
devanagari: यावताचार्य - गृहे निमाञि र अवस्थान ।
मुञि भिक्षा दिमु, सबाकारे मागों दान ॥171॥
cc-madhya-3.171.translation: Mother Śacī appealed to all the devotees to give her this charity: As long as Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu remained at the house of Advaita Ācārya, only she would supply Him food.

lines: mātāra ye icchā sei sammata sabāra
devanagari: शुनि’ भक्तगण कहे क रि’ नमस्कार ।
मातार ये इच्छा सेइ सम्मत सबार ॥172॥
cc-madhya-3.172.translation: Hearing this appeal from mother Śacī, all the devotees offered obeisances and said, "We all agree to whatever mother Śacī desires."

lines: mātāra vyagratā dekhi' prabhura vyagra mana
devanagari: मातार व्यग्रता देखि’ प्रभुर व्यग्र मन ।
भक्त - गण एकत्र क रि’ बलिला वचन ॥173॥
cc-madhya-3.173.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu saw His mother's great eagerness, He became a little agitated. He therefore assembled all the devotees present and spoke to them.

devanagari: तोमा - सबार आज्ञा विना चलिलाम वृन्दावन ।
याइते नारिल, विघ्न कैल निवर्तन ॥174॥
cc-madhya-3.174.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu informed them all, "Without your order, I tried to go to Vṛndāvana. There was some obstacle, however, and I had to return.

devanagari: यद्यपि सहसा आमि करियाछि सन्न्यास ।
तथापि तोमा - सबा हैते नहिब उदास ॥175॥
cc-madhya-3.175.translation: "My dear friends, although I have suddenly accepted this renounced order, I still know that I shall never be indifferent to you.

lines: tomā-saba nā chāḍiba, yāvat āmi jība'
devanagari: तोमा - सब ना छाड़िब, यावतामि जीब’ ।
मातारे तावतामि छाड़िते नारिब ॥176॥
cc-madhya-3.176.translation: "My dear friends, as long as I remain manifest, I shall never give you up. Nor shall I be able to give up My mother.

devanagari: सन्न्यासीर धर्म नहे - सन्न्यास करिञा ।
निज जन्म - स्थाने रहे कुटुम्ब लञा ॥177॥
cc-madhya-3.177.translation: "After accepting sannyāsa, it is not the duty of a sannyāsī to remain at his birthplace, encircled by relatives.

lines: keha yena ei bali' nā kare nindana
sei yukti kaha, yāte rahe dui dharma
devanagari: केह येन एइ ब लि’ ना करे निन्दन ।
सेइ मुक्ति कह, याते रहे दुइ धर्म ॥178॥
cc-madhya-3.178.translation: "Make some arrangement so that I may not leave you and at the same time people may not blame Me for remaining with relatives after taking sannyāsa."

devanagari: शुनिया प्रभुर एइ मधुर वचन ।
शची - पाश आचार्यादि करिल गमन ॥179॥
cc-madhya-3.179.translation: After hearing Lord Caitanya's statement, all the devotees, headed by Advaita Ācārya, approached mother Śacī.

lines: kaha dekhi, kon pathe yāba vṛndāvana'
devanagari: तबे प्रभु पुछिलेन, - ‘शुन, शिशु - गण ।
कह देखि, कोन्पथे याब वृन्दावन’ ॥18॥
cc-madhya-3.18-19.translation: When the cowherd boys were questioned by Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu about the path to Vṛndāvana, the boys showed Him the path on the bank of the Ganges, and the Lord went that way in ecstasy.

devanagari: प्रभुर निवेदन ताँरे सकल कहिल ।
शुनि’ शची जगन्माता कहते लागिल ॥180॥
cc-madhya-3.180.translation: When they submitted Lord Caitanya's statement, mother Śacī, who is the mother of the universe, began to speak.

lines: teṅho yadi ihāṅ rahe, tabe mora sukha
tāṅ'ra nindā haya yadi, seha mora duḥkha
devanagari: तेंहो यदि इहाँ रहे, तबे मोर सुख ।
ताँ’र निन्दा हय यदि, सेह मोर दुःख ॥181॥
cc-madhya-3.181.translation: Śacīmātā said, "It will be a great happiness for me if Nimāi, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, stays here. But at the same time, if someone blames Him, it will be my great unhappiness."

lines: tāte ei yukti bhāla, mora mane laya
nīlācale rahe yadi, dui kārya haya
devanagari: ताते एइ युक्ति भाल, मोर मने लय ।
नीलाचले रहे यदि, दुइ कार्य हय ॥182॥
cc-madhya-3.182.translation: Mother Śacī said, "This consideration is good. In my opinion, if Nimāi remains at Jagannātha Purī, He may not leave any one of us and at the same time can remain aloof as a sannyāsī. Thus both purposes are fulfilled.

devanagari: नीलाचले नवद्वीपे येन दुइ घर ।
लोक - गतागति - वार्ता पाब निरन्तर ॥183॥
cc-madhya-3.183.translation: "Since Jagannātha Purī and Navadvīpa are intimately related-as if they were two rooms in the same house-people from Navadvīpa generally go to Jagannātha Purī, and those in Jagannātha Purī go to Navadvīpa. This going and coming will help carry news of Lord Caitanya. In this way I will be able to get news of Him.

devanagari: तुमि सब करिते पार गमनागमन ।
गङ्गा - स्नाने कभु हबे ताँर आगमन ॥184॥
cc-madhya-3.184.translation: "All you devotees will be able to come and go, and sometimes He may also come to take His bath in the Ganges.

lines: tāṅra yei sukha, tāhā nija-sukha māni
devanagari: आपनार दुःख - सुख ताहाँ नाहि गणि ।
ताँर येइ सुख, ताहा निज - सुख मानि ॥185॥
cc-madhya-3.185.translation: "I do not care for my personal happiness or unhappiness, but only for His happiness. Indeed, I accept His happiness as my happiness."

devanagari: शुनि’ भक्त - गण ताँरे करिल स्तवन ।
वेद - आज्ञा यैछे, माता, तोमार वचन ॥186॥
cc-madhya-3.186.translation: After hearing Śacīmātā, all the devotees offered her prayers and assured her that her order, like a Vedic injunction, could not be violated.

devanagari: भक्त - गण प्रभु - आगे आसिया कहिल ।
शुनिया प्रभुर मने आनन्द हइल ॥187॥
cc-madhya-3.187.translation: All the devotees informed Lord Caitanya of Śacīmātā's decision. Hearing it, the Lord became very pleased.

devanagari: नवद्वीप - वासी आदि यत भक्त - गण ।
सबारे सम्मान करि बलिला वचन ॥188॥
cc-madhya-3.188.translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered respects to all the devotees present from Navadvīpa and other towns, speaking to them as follows.

lines: ei bhikṣā māgoṅ,—more deha tumi saba
devanagari: तुमि - सब लोक - मोर परम बान्धव ।
एइ भिक्षा मागों , - मोरे देह तुमि सब ॥189॥
cc-madhya-3.189.translation: "My dear friends, you are all My intimate friends. Now I am begging a favor of you. Please give it to Me."

devanagari: घरे या ञा कर सदा कृष्ण - सङ्कीर्तन ।
कृष्ण - नाम, कृष्ण - कथा, कृष्ण आराधन ॥190॥
cc-madhya-3.190.translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested them all to return home and begin chanting the holy name congregationally. He also requested them to worship Kṛṣṇa, chant His holy name and discuss His holy pastimes.

lines: madhye madhye āsi' tomāya diba daraśana
devanagari: आज्ञा देह नीलाचले करिये गमन ।
मध्ये मध्ये आ सि’ तोमाय दिब दरशन ॥191॥
cc-madhya-3.191.translation: After thus instructing the devotees, the Lord asked their permission to go to Jagannātha Purī. He assured them that at intervals He would come there and meet them again and again.

devanagari: एत ब लि’ सबाकारे ईषत् हासिञा ।
विदाय करिल प्रभु सम्मान करिञा ॥192॥
cc-madhya-3.192.translation: In this way, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, offering due respects to all the devotees and smiling very mildly, bid them farewell.

lines: sabā vidāya diyā prabhu calite kaila mana
devanagari: सबा विदाय दिया प्रभु चलिते कैल मन ।
हरिदास का न्दि’ कहे करुण वचन ॥193॥
cc-madhya-3.193.translation: After requesting all the devotees to return home, the Lord decided to go to Jagannātha Purī. At that time Haridāsa Ṭhākura began to cry and speak some pathetic words.

lines: nīlācale yābe tumi, mora kon gati
devanagari: नीलाचले याबे तुमि, मोर कोन्गति ।
नीलाचले याइते मोर नाहिक शकति ॥194॥
cc-madhya-3.194.translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "You are going to Jagannātha Purī, and that is all right, but what will be my destination? I am not able to go to Jagannātha Purī."

lines: muñi adhama tomāra nā pāba daraśana
devanagari: मुञि अधम तोमार ना पाब दरशन ।
केमते धरिब एइ पापिष्ठ जीवन ॥195॥
cc-madhya-3.195.translation: "Because I am the lowest among men, I shall not be able to see You. How shall I maintain my sinful life?"

lines: tomāra dainyete mora vyākula haya mana
devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - कर तुमि दैन्य सम्वरण ।
तोमार दैन्येते मोर व्याकुल हय मन ॥196॥
cc-madhya-3.196.translation: The Lord replied to Haridāsa Ṭhākura, "Please check your humility. Just by seeing your humility, my mind becomes very much agitated."

devanagari: तोमा ला गि’ जगन्नाथे करिब निवेदन ।
तोमा - लञा याब आमि श्री - पुरुषोत्तम ॥197॥
cc-madhya-3.197.translation: Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu assured Haridāsa Ṭhākura that He would place a petition before Lord Jagannātha and that He would certainly take him there to Jagannātha Purī.

lines: tabe ta' ācārya kahe vinaya kariñā
dina dui-cāri raha kṛpā ta' kariñā
devanagari: तबे त’ आचार्य कहे विनय करिञा ।
दिन दुइ - चारि रह कृपा त’ करिञा ॥198॥
cc-madhya-3.198.translation: After that, Advaita Ācārya respectfully requested Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu to show Him mercy by remaining another two or four days.

lines: ācāryera vākya prabhu nā kare laṅghana
devanagari: आचार्येर वाक्य प्रभु ना करे लङ्घन ।
रहिला अद्वैत - गृहे, ना कैल गमन ॥199॥
cc-madhya-3.199.translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu never violated the request of Advaita Ācārya; therefore He remained at His home and did not leave immediately for Jagannātha Purī.

devanagari: जय जय श्री - चैतन्य जय नित्यानन्द ।
जयाद्वैतचन्द्र जय गौर - भक्त - वृन्द ॥2॥
cc-madhya-3.2.translation: All glories to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda! All glories to Advaita Prabhu! And all glories to the devotees of Lord Caitanya, headed by Śrīvāsa!

devanagari: आचार्य रत्नेरे कहे नित्यानन्द - गोसाञि ।
शीघ्र याह तुमि अद्वैत - आचार्येर ठाञि ॥20॥
cc-madhya-3.20.translation: As the Lord proceeded along the bank of the Ganges, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu requested Ācāryaratna [Candraśekhara Ācārya] to go immediately to the house of Advaita Ācārya.

lines: ānandita haila ācārya, śacī, bhakta, saba
devanagari: आनन्दित हैल आचार्य, शची, भक्त, सब ।
प्रति - दिन करे आचार्य महा - महोत्सव ॥200॥
cc-madhya-3.200.translation: Lord Caitanya's decision was received very happily by Advaita Ācārya, mother Śacī and all the devotees. Advaita Ācārya celebrated every day with a great festival.

devanagari: दिने कृष्ण - कथा - रस भक्त - गण - सङ्गे ।
रात्रे महा - महोत्सव सङ्कीर्तन - रङ्गे ॥201॥
cc-madhya-3.201.translation: During the day the devotees discussed subject matters concerning Kṛṣṇa, and at night there was a great festival of congregational chanting at the house of Advaita Ācārya.

lines: sukhe bhojana kare prabhu lañā bhakta-gaṇa
devanagari: आनन्दित ह ञा शची करेन रन्धन ।
सुखे भोजन करे प्रभु लञा भक्त - गण ॥202॥
cc-madhya-3.202.translation: Mother Śacī cooked with great pleasure, and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, along with the devotees, accepted the prasāda with great pleasure.

devanagari: आचार्येर श्रद्धा - भक्ति - गृह - सम्पद - धने ।
सकल सफल हैल प्रभुर आराधने ॥203॥
cc-madhya-3.203.translation: In this way all the opulences of Advaita Ācārya-His faith, devotion, home, riches and everything else-were successfully utilized in the worship of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

devanagari: शचीर आनन्द बाड़े देखि’ पुत्र - मुख ।
भोजन करा ञा पूर्ण कैल निज - सुख ॥204॥
cc-madhya-3.204.translation: As mother Śacī constantly saw the face of her son and fed Him, her own happiness increased and was indeed complete.

devanagari: एइ - मत अद्वैत - गृहे भक्त - गण मिले ।
वञ्चिला कतक - दिन महा - कुतूहले ॥205॥
cc-madhya-3.205.translation: In this way, at Advaita Ācārya's house all the devotees met and passed some days together in a greatly festive mood.

lines: āra dina prabhu kahe saba bhakta-gaṇe
devanagari: आर दिन प्रभु कहे सब भक्त - गणे ।
निज - निज - गृहे सबे करह गमने ॥206॥
cc-madhya-3.206.translation: The next day, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu requested all the devotees to return to their respective homes.

devanagari: घरे गिया कर सबे कृष्ण - सङ्कीर्तन ।
पुनरपि आमा - सङ्गे हइबे मिलन ॥207॥
cc-madhya-3.207.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu also asked them to execute the congregational chanting of the holy name of the Lord at their homes, and He assured them that they would be able to meet Him again.

lines: kabhu vā tomarā karibe nīlādri gamana
kabhu vā āsiba āmi karite gaṅgā-snāna
devanagari: कभु वा तोमरा करिबे नीलाद्रि गमन ।
कभु वा आसिब आमि करिते गङ्गा - स्नान ॥208॥
cc-madhya-3.208.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu told them, "Sometimes you will come to Jagannātha Purī, and sometimes I shall come bathe in the Ganges."

devanagari: नित्यानन्द - गोसाञि, पण्डित जगदानन्द ।
दामोदर पण्डित, आर दत्त मुकुन्द ॥209॥
cc-madhya-3.209-210.translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya sent four persons-Nityānanda Gosāñi, Jagadānanda Paṇḍita, Dāmodara Paṇḍita and Mukunda Datta-to accompany the Lord. After pacifying His mother, Śacīmātā, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu submitted prayers to her lotus feet.

lines: prabhu laye yāba āmi tāṅhāra mandire
sāvadhāne rahena yena naukā lañā tīre
devanagari: प्रभु लये याब आमि ताँहार मन्दिरे ।
सावधाने रहेन येन नौका लञा तीरे ॥21॥
cc-madhya-3.21.translation: Śrī Nityānanda Gosvāmī told him, "I shall take Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to the bank of the Ganges at Śāntipura, and Advaita Ācārya should carefully stay there on shore with a boat.

devanagari: ताँरे प्रदक्षिण क रि’ करिल गमन ।
एथा आचार्येर घरे उठिल क्रन्दन ॥211॥
cc-madhya-3.211.translation: When everything was arranged, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu circumambulated His mother and then started for Jagannātha Purī. In the house of Advaita Ācārya there arose tumultuous crying.

devanagari: निरपेक्ष ह ञा प्रभु शीघ्र चलिला ।
कान्दिते कान्दिते आचार्य पश्चात्चलिला ॥212॥
cc-madhya-3.212.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was unaffected. He left swiftly, and Advaita Ācārya followed Him weeping.

lines: kata dūra giyā prabhu kari' yoḍa hāta
ācārye prabodhi' kahe kichu miṣṭa bāta
devanagari: कत दूर गिया प्रभु करि’ योड़ हात ।
आचार्ये प्रबो धि’ कहे किछु मिष्ट बात ॥213॥
cc-madhya-3.213.translation: After He had followed Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu for some distance, Advaita Ācārya was petitioned by Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu with folded hands. The Lord spoke the following sweet words.

lines: tumi vyagra haile kāro nā rahibe prāṇa
devanagari: जननी प्रबो धि’ कर भक्त समाधान ।
तुमि व्यग्र हैले कारो ना रहिबे प्राण ॥214॥
cc-madhya-3.214.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Please pacify all the devotees and My mother. If You become agitated, no one will be able to continue to exist."

lines: eta bali' prabhu tāṅre kari' āliṅgana
devanagari: एत ब लि’ प्रभु ताँरे करि’ आलिङ्गन ।
निवृत्ति करिया कैल स्वच्छन्द गमन ॥215॥
cc-madhya-3.215.translation: Saying this, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu embraced Advaita Ācārya and stopped Him from following any further. Then, without anxiety, He proceeded to Jagannātha Purī.

devanagari: गङ्गा - तीरे - तीरे प्रभु चारि - जन - साथे ।
नीलाद्रि चलिला प्रभु छत्रभोग - पथे ॥216॥
cc-madhya-3.216.translation: The Lord, with the other four persons, went along the banks of the Ganges through the path of Chatrabhoga toward Nīlādri, Jagannātha Purī.

devanagari: ‘चैतन्य - मङ्गले’ प्रभुर नीलाद्रि - गमन ।
विस्तारि वर्णियाछेन दास - वृन्दावन ॥217॥
cc-madhya-3.217.translation: In his book known as Caitanya-maṅgala [Caitanya-bhāgavata], Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura has elaborately described the Lord's passage to Jagannātha Purī.

lines: advaita-gṛhe prabhura vilāsa śune yei jana
devanagari: अद्वैत - गृहे प्रभुर विलास शुने येइ जन ।
अचिरे मिलये ताँरे कृष्ण - प्रेम - धन ॥218॥
cc-madhya-3.218.translation: If one hears the activities of the Lord at the house of Advaita Ācārya, he will certainly very soon attain the riches of love of Kṛṣṇa.

devanagari: श्री - रूप - रघुनाथ - पदे यार आश ।
चैतन्य - चरितामृत कहे कृष्णदास ॥219॥
cc-madhya-3.219.translation: Praying at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, always desiring their mercy, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta, following in their footsteps.

devanagari: तबे नवद्वीपे तुमि करिह गमन ।
शची - सह लञा आइस सब भक्त - गण ॥22॥
cc-madhya-3.22.translation: "After that," Nityānanda Prabhu continued, "I shall go to Advaita Ācārya's house, and you should go to Navadvīpa and return with mother Śacī and all the other devotees."

devanagari: ताँरे पाठाइया नित्यानन्द महाशय ।
महाप्रभुर आगे आसि’ दिल परिचय ॥23॥
cc-madhya-3.23.translation: After sending Ācāryaratna to the house of Advaita Ācārya, Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu went before Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and gave notice of His coming.

lines: śrīpāda kahe, tomāra saṅge yāba vṛndāvana
devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - श्रीपाद, तोमार कोथाके गमन ।
श्रीपाद कहे, तोमार सङ्गे याब वृन्दावन ॥24॥
cc-madhya-3.24.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was in ecstasy, and He asked where Nityānanda Prabhu was going. Nityānanda replied that He was going with Him toward Vṛndāvana.

devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - कत दूरे आछे वृन्दावन ।
तेंहो कहेन , - कर एइ यमुना दरशन ॥25॥
cc-madhya-3.25.translation: When the Lord asked Nityānanda Prabhu how far it was to Vṛndāvana, Nityānanda replied, "Just see! Here is the river Yamunā."

devanagari: एत बलि’ आनिल ताँरे गङ्गा - सन्निधाने ।
आवेशे प्रभुर हैल गङ्गारे यमुना - ज्ञाने ॥26॥
cc-madhya-3.26.translation: Saying this, Nityānanda Prabhu took Caitanya Mahāprabhu near the Ganges, and the Lord, in His ecstasy, accepted the river Ganges as the river Yamunā.

devanagari: अहो भाग्य, यमुनारे पाइलुँ दरशन ।
एत ब लि’ यमुनार करेन स्तवन ॥27॥
cc-madhya-3.27.translation: The Lord said, "Oh, what good fortune! Now I have seen the river Yamunā." Thus thinking the Ganges to be the river Yamunā, Caitanya Mahāprabhu began to offer prayers to it.

devanagari: चिदानन्द - भानोः सदा नन्द - सूनोः पर - प्रेम - पात्री द्रव - ब्रह्म - गात्री ।
अघानां लवित्री जगत्क्षेम - धात्री पवित्री - क्रियान्नो वपुर्मित्र - पुत्री ॥28॥
cc-madhya-3.28.translation: "O river Yamunā, you are the blissful spiritual water that gives love to the son of Nanda Mahārāja. You are the same as the water of the spiritual world, for you can vanquish all our offenses and the sinful reactions incurred in life. You are the creator of all auspicious things for the world. O daughter of the son-god, kindly purify us by your pious activities."

devanagari: एत ब लि’ नमस्क रि’ कैल गङ्गा - स्नान ।
एक कौपीन, नाहि द्वितीय परिधान ॥29॥
cc-madhya-3.29.translation: After reciting this mantra, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered obeisances and took His bath in the Ganges. At that time He had on only one piece of underwear, for there was no second garment.

devanagari: चब्बिश वत्सर - शेष येइ माघ - मास ।
तार शुक्ल पक्षे प्रभु करिला सन्न्यास ॥3॥
cc-madhya-3.3.translation: At the end of His twenty-fourth year, in the month of Māgha, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accepted the sannyāsa order during the waxing period of the moon.

devanagari: हेन काले आचार्य - गोसाञि नौकाते चड़िञा ।
आइल नूतन कौपीन - बहिर्वास लञा ॥30॥
cc-madhya-3.30.translation: While Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was standing there without a second garment, Śrī Advaita Ācārya arrived on a boat, bringing with Him new underwear and external garments.

lines: āge ācārya āsi' rahilā namaskāra kari'
ācārya dekhi' bale prabhu mane saṁśaya kari'
devanagari: आगे आचार्य आ सि’ रहिला नमस्कार क रि’ ।
आचार्य देखि’ बले प्रभु मने संशय करि’ ॥31॥
cc-madhya-3.31.translation: When Advaita Ācārya arrived, He stood before the Lord and offered His obeisances. After seeing Him, the Lord began to wonder about the entire situation.

lines: tumi ta' ācārya-gosāñi, ethā kene āilā
devanagari: तुमि त’ आचार्य - गोसाञि, एथा केने आइला ।
आमि वृन्दावने, तुमि के - मते जानिला ॥32॥
cc-madhya-3.32.translation: Still in His ecstasy, the Lord asked Advaita Ācārya, "Why did You come here? How did You know that I was in Vṛndāvana?"

devanagari: आचार्य कहे - तुमि याहाँ, सेइ वृन्दावन ।
मोर भाग्ये गङ्गा - तीरे तोमार आगमन ॥33॥
cc-madhya-3.33.translation: Advaita Ācārya disclosed the whole situation, telling Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, "Wherever You are, that is Vṛndāvana. Now it is My great fortune that You have come to the bank of the Ganges."

devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - नित्यानन्द आमारे वञ्चिला ।
गङ्गाके आनिया मोरे यमुना कहिला ॥34॥
cc-madhya-3.34.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu then said, "Nityānanda has cheated Me. He has brought Me to the bank of the Ganges and told Me that it was the Yamunā."

devanagari: आचार्य कहे, मिथ्या नहे श्रीपाद - वचन ।
यमुनाते स्नान तुमि करिला एखन ॥35॥
cc-madhya-3.35.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu accused Nityānanda of cheating Him, Śrīla Advaita Ācārya said, "Whatever Nityānanda Prabhu has told You is not false. You have indeed just now taken Your bath in the river Yamunā."

devanagari: गङ्गाय यमुना वहे हञा एक - धार ।
पश्चिमे यमुना वहे, पूर्वे गङ्गा - धार ॥36॥
cc-madhya-3.36.translation: Advaita Ācārya then explained that at that spot both the Ganges and Yamunā flow together. On the western side was the Yamunā, and on the eastern side was the Ganges.

lines: paścima-dhāre yamunā vahe, tāhāṅ kaile snāna
ārdra kaupīna chāḍi' śuṣka kara paridhāna
devanagari: पश्चिम - धारे यमुना वहे, ताहाँ कैले स्नान ।
आर्द्र कौपीन छा ड़ि’ शुष्क कर परिधान ॥37॥
cc-madhya-3.37.translation: Advaita Ācārya then suggested that since Caitanya Mahāprabhu had taken His bath in the river Yamunā and His underwear was now wet, the Lord should change His underwear for dry garments.

lines: āji mora ghare bhikṣā, cala mora vāsa
devanagari: प्रेमावेशे तिन दिन आछ उपवास ।
आजि मोर घरे भिक्षा, चल मोर वास ॥38॥
cc-madhya-3.38.translation: Advaita Ācārya said, "You have been fasting continuously for three days in Your ecstasy of love for Kṛṣṇa. I therefore invite You to My home, where You may kindly take Your alms. Come with Me to My residence."

lines: śukhārukhā vyañjana kailuṅ, sūpa āra śāka
devanagari: एक - मुष्टि अन्न मुञि करियाछों पाक ।
शुखारुखा व्यञ्जन कैलुँ, सूप आर शाक ॥39॥
cc-madhya-3.39.translation: Advaita Prabhu continued, "At My home I have just cooked one palmful of rice. The vetetables are always very simple. There is no luxurious cooking-simply a little liquid vegetable and spinach."

devanagari: सन्न्यास करि’ प्रेमावेशे चलिला वृन्दावन ।
राढ़ - देशे तिन दिन करिला भ्रमण ॥4॥
cc-madhya-3.4.translation: After accepting the sannyāsa order, Caitanya Mahāprabhu, out of intense love for Kṛṣṇa, started for Vṛndāvana. However, He mistakenly wandered about in a trance continuously for three days in the tract of land known as Rāḍha-deśa.

lines: eta bali' naukāya caḍāñā nila nija-ghara
devanagari: एत ब लि’ नौकाय चड़ा ञा निल निज - घर ।
पाद - प्रक्षालन कैल आनन्द - अन्तर ॥40॥
cc-madhya-3.40.translation: Saying this, Śrī Advaita Ācārya took the Lord into the boat and brought the Lord to His residence. There Advaita Ācārya washed the feet of the Lord and was consequently very happy within.

devanagari: प्रथमे पाक करियाछेन आचार्याणी ।
विष्णु - समर्पण कैल आचार्य आपनि ॥41॥
cc-madhya-3.41.translation: All the eatables were first cooked by the wife of Advaita Ācārya. Then Śrīla Advaita Ācārya personally offered everything to Lord Viṣṇu.

lines: tina ṭhāñi bhoga bāḍāila sama kari'
devanagari: तिन ठाञि भोग बाड़ाइल सम क रि’ ।
कृष्णेर भोग बाड़ाइल धातु - पात्रोपरि ॥42॥
cc-madhya-3.42.translation: All the prepared foods were divided into three equal parts. One part was arranged on a metal plate for offering to Lord Kṛṣṇa.

lines: dui ṭhāñi bhoga bāḍāila bhāla mate
devanagari: बत्तिशा - आठिया - कलार आङ्गटिया पाते ।
दुइ ठाञि भोग बाड़ाइल भाल मते ॥43॥
cc-madhya-3.43.translation: Of the three divisions, one was arranged on a metal plate, and the other two were arranged on plantain leaves. These leaves were not bifurcated, and they were taken from a banana tree that held at least thirty-two bunches of bananas. The two plates were filled very nicely with the kinds of food described below.

devanagari: मध्ये पीत - घृत - सिक्त शाल्यन्नेर स्तूप ।
चारि - दिके व्यञ्जन - डोङ्गा, आर मुद्ग - सूप ॥44॥
cc-madhya-3.44.translation: The cooked rice was a stack of very fine grains nicely cooked, and in the middle was yellow butter clarified from the milk of cows. Surrounding the stack of rice were pots made of the skins of banana trees, and in these pots were varieties of vegetables and mung dāl.

devanagari: सार्द्रक, वास्तुक - शाक विविध प्रकार ।
पटोल, कुष्माण्ड - बड़ि, मानकचु आर ॥45॥
cc-madhya-3.45.translation: Among the cooked vegetables were paṭolas, squash, mānakacu and a salad made with pieces of ginger and various types of spinach.

devanagari: चइ - मरिच - सुख्त दिया सब फल - मूले ।
अमृत - निन्दक पञ्च - विध तिक्त - झाले ॥46॥
cc-madhya-3.46.translation: There was sukhta, bitter melon mixed with all kinds of vegetables, defying the taste of nectar. There were five types of bitter and pungent sukhtas.

devanagari: कोमल निम्ब - पत्र सह भा जा वार्ताकी ।
पटोल - फुल - बड़ि - भाजा, कुष्माण्ड - मानचाकि ॥47॥
cc-madhya-3.47.translation: Amongst the various vegetables were newly grown leaves of nimba trees fried with eggplant. The fruit known as paṭola was fried with phulabaḍi, a kind of dahl preparation first mashed and then dried in the sun. There was also a preparation known as kuṣmāṇḍa-mānacāki.

devanagari: नारिकेल - शस्य, छाना, शर्करा मधुर ।
मोचा - घण्ट, दुग्ध - कुष्माण्ड, सकल प्रचुर ॥48॥
cc-madhya-3.48.translation: The preparation made with coconut pulp mixed with curd and rock candy was very sweet. There was a curry made of banana flowers and squash boiled in milk, all in great quantity.

lines: sakala vyañjana kaila loke yata haya
devanagari: मधुराम्ल - बड़ा, अम्लादि पाँच - छय ।
सकल व्यञ्जन कैल लोके यत हय ॥49॥
cc-madhya-3.49.translation: There were small cakes in sweet and sour sauce and five or six kinds of sour preparations. All the vegetables were so made that everyone present could take prasāda.

lines: ei śloka paḍi' prabhu bhāvera āveśe
devanagari: एइ श्लोक प ड़ि’ प्रभु भावेर आवेशे ।
भ्रमिते पवित्र कैल सब राढ़ - देशे ॥5॥
cc-madhya-3.5.translation: Passing through the tract of land known as Rāḍha-deśa, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited the following verse in ecstasy.

devanagari: मुद्ग - बड़ा, कला - बड़ा, माष - बड़ा, मिष्ट ।
क्षीर - पुली, नारिकेल, यत पिठा इष्ट ॥50॥
cc-madhya-3.50.translation: There were soft cakes made with mung dahl, soft cakes made with ripe bananas, and soft cakes made with urd dahl. There were various kinds of sweetmeats, condensed milk mixed with rice cakes, a coconut preparation and every kind of cake desirable.

lines: cale hāle nāhi,—ḍoṅgā ati baḍa daḍa
devanagari: बत्तिशा - आठिया कलार डोङ्गा बड़ बड़।
चले हाले नाहि , - डोङ्गा अति बड़ दड़ ॥51॥
cc-madhya-3.51.translation: All the vegetables were served in pots made of banana leaves taken from trees producing at least thirty-two bunches of bananas. These pots were very strong and big and did not tilt or totter.

lines: tina bhogera āśe pāśe rākhila dhariñā
devanagari: पञ्चाश पञ्चाश डोङ्गा व्यञ्जने पूरिञा ।
तिन भोगेर आशे पाशे राखिल धरिञा ॥52॥
cc-madhya-3.52.translation: All around the three eating places were a hundred pots filled with various kinds of vegetables.

devanagari: सघृत - पायस नव - मृत्कुण्डिका भरिञा ।
तिन पात्रे घनावर्त - दुग्ध राखेत धरिञा ॥53॥
cc-madhya-3.53.translation: Along with the various vegetables was sweet rice mixed with ghee. This was kept in new earthen pots. Earthen pots filled with highly condensed milk were placed in three places.

lines: yateka karila' tāhā kahite nā śaki
devanagari: दुग्ध - चिड़ा - कला आर दुग्ध - लक्लकी ।
यतेक करिल’ ताहा कहिते ना शकि ॥54॥
cc-madhya-3.54.translation: Besides the other preparations, there were chipped rice made with milk and mixed with bananas, and also white squash boiled in milk. Indeed, it is not possible to describe all the preparations that were made.

lines: dui pāśe dharila saba mṛt-kuṇḍikā bhari'
devanagari: दुइ पाशे धरिल सब मृत्कुण्डिका भरि’ ।
चाँपाकला - दधि - सन्देश कहिते ना पारि ॥55॥
cc-madhya-3.55.translation: In two places there were earthen pots filled with another preparation made with yogurt, sandeśa [a sweetmeat made with curd] and banana. I am unable to describe it all.

devanagari: अन्न - व्यञ्जन - उपरि दिल तुलसी - मञ्जरी ।
तिन जल - पात्रे सुवासित जल भरि’ ॥56॥
cc-madhya-3.56.translation: Upon the stack of boiled rice and all the vegetables were flowers of the tulasī trees. There were also pots filled with scented rosewater.

devanagari: तिन शुभ्र - पीठ, तार उपरि वसन ।
एइ - रूपे साक्षात्कृष्णे कराइल भोजन ॥57॥
cc-madhya-3.57.translation: There were three sitting places where soft cloths were placed. Thus Lord Kṛṣṇa was offered all the foodstuff, and the Lord took it very pleasantly.

devanagari: आरतिर काले दुइ प्रभु बोलाइल ।
प्रभु - सङ्गे सबे आ सि’ आरति देखिल ॥58॥
cc-madhya-3.58.translation: It is the system, after offering food, to perform bhoga-ārati. Advaita Prabhu asked the two brothers, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu, to come see the ārati. The two Lords and all others present went to see the ārati ceremony.

lines: ācārya āsi' prabhure tabe kailā nivedana
devanagari: आरति करिया कृष्णे करा’ल शयन ।
आचार्य आ सि’ प्रभुरे तबे कैला निवेदन ॥59॥
cc-madhya-3.59.translation: After ārati was performed for the Deities in the temple, Lord Kṛṣṇa was made to lie down to rest. Advaita Ācārya then came out to submit something to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

devanagari: एतां स आस्थाय परात्म - निष्ठाम् अध्यासितां पूर्वतमैर्महद्भिः ।
अहं तरिष्यामि दुरन्त - पारं तमो मुकुन्दाघ्रि - निषेवयैव ॥6॥
cc-madhya-3.6.translation: "[As a brāhmaṇa from Avantī-deśa said:] 'I shall cross over the insurmountable ocean of nescience by being firmly fixed in the service of the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. This was approved by the previous ācāryas, who were fixed in firm devotion to the Lord, Paramātmā, the Supreme Personality of Godhead."

lines: dui bhāi āilā tabe karite bhojana
devanagari: गृहेर भितरे प्रभु करुन गमन ।
दुइ भाइ आइला तबे करिते भोजन ॥60॥
cc-madhya-3.60.translation: Śrī Advaita Prabhu said, "My dear Lords, kindly enter this room." The two brothers, Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu, then came forward to take the prasāda.

devanagari: मुकुन्द, हरिदास, - दुइ प्रभु बोलाइल ।
योड़ - हाते दुइ - जन कहिते लागिल ॥61॥
cc-madhya-3.61.translation: When Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Nityānanda Prabhu went to accept the prasāda, They both called Mukunda and Haridāsa to come with Them. However, Mukunda and Haridāsa, both with folded hands, spoke as follows.

lines: mukunda kahe—mora kichu kṛtya nāhi sare
pāche muñi prasāda pāmu, tumi yāha ghare
devanagari: मुकुन्द कहे - मोर किछु कृत्य नाहि सरे ।
पाछे मुञि प्रसाद पामु, तुमि याह घरे ॥62॥
cc-madhya-3.62.translation: When Mukunda was called for, he submitted, "My dear sir, I have something to do that is not yet finished. Later I shall accept the prasāda, so You two Prabhus should now please enter the room."

lines: bāhire eka muṣṭi pāche karimu bhojana
devanagari: हरिदास कहे - मुञि पापिष्ठ अधम ।
बाहिरे एक मुष्टि पाछे करिमु भोजन ॥63॥
cc-madhya-3.63.translation: Haridāsa Ṭhākura said, "I am the most sinful and lowest among men. Later I shall eat one palmful of prasāda while waiting outside."

lines: dui prabhu lañā ācārya gelā bhitara ghare
devanagari: दुइ प्रभु लञा आचार्य गेला भितर घरे ।
प्रसाद देखिया प्रभुर आनन्द अन्तरे ॥64॥
cc-madhya-3.64.translation: Advaita Ācārya took Lord Nityānanda Prabhu and Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu within the room, and the two Lords saw the arrangement of the prasāda. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was especially very much pleased.

lines: aiche anna ye kṛṣṇake karāya bhojana
janme janme śire dharoṅ tāṅhāra caraṇa
devanagari: ऐछे अन्न ये कृष्णके कराय भोजन ।
जन्मे जन्मे शिरे धरों ताँहार चरण ॥65॥
cc-madhya-3.65.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved of all the methods employed in cooking and offering food to Kṛṣṇa. Indeed, He was so pleased that He said, "Frankly, I will personally take the lotus feet of anyone who can offer Kṛṣṇa such nice food and place those lotus feet on My head birth after birth."

devanagari: प्रभु जाने तिन भोग - कृष्णेर नैवेद्य ।
आचार्सेर मनः - कथा नहे प्रभुर वेद्य ॥66॥
cc-madhya-3.66.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu entered the room, He saw three divisions of food, and He knew that all of these were meant for Kṛṣṇa. However, He did not understand the intentions of Advaita Ācārya.

devanagari: प्रभु बले - वैस तिने करिये भोजन ।
आचार्य कहे - आमि करिब परिवेशन ॥67॥
cc-madhya-3.67.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Let Us sit down in these three places, and We shall take prasāda." However, Advaita Ācārya said, "I shall distribute the prasāda."

lines: kon sthāne vasiba, āra āna dui pāta
alpa kari' āni' tāhe deha vyañjana bhāta
devanagari: कोन् स्थाने वसिब, आर आन दुइ पात ।
अल्प क रि’ आनि’ ताहे देह व्यञ्जन भात ॥68॥
cc-madhya-3.68.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu thought that all three servings were meant for distribution; therefore He asked for another two banana leaves, saying, "Let Us have a very little quantity of vegetable and rice."

lines: eta bali' hāte dhari' vasāila duṅhāre
devanagari: आचार्य कहे - वैस दोहे पिंड़िर उपरे ।
एत ब लि’ हाते ध रि’ वसाइल दुँहारे ॥69॥
cc-madhya-3.69.translation: Advaita Ācārya said, "Just sit down here on these seats." Catching Their hands, He sat Them both down.

devanagari: प्रभु कहे - साधु एइ भिक्षुर वचन ।
मुकुन्द सेवन - व्रत कैल निर्धारण ॥7॥
cc-madhya-3.7.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu approved the purport of this verse on account of the determination of the mendicant devotee to engage in the service of Lord Mukunda. He gave His approval of this verse, indicating that it was very good.

lines: ihā khāile kaiche haya indriya vāraṇa
devanagari: प्रभु कहे - सन्न्यासीर भक्ष्य नहे उपकरण ।
इहा खाइले कैछे हय इन्द्रिय वारण ॥70॥
cc-madhya-3.70.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "It is not proper for a sannyāsī to eat such a variety of foodstuff. If he does, how can he control his senses?"

lines: āmi saba jāni tomāra sannyāsera bhāri-bhuri
devanagari: आचार्य कहे - छाड़ तुमि आपनार चुरि ।
आमि सब जानि तोमार सन्यासेर भारि - भूरि ॥71॥
cc-madhya-3.71.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not accept the food that had already been served, Advaita Ācārya said, "Please give up Your concealment. I know what You are, and I know the confidential meaning of Your accepting the sannyāsa order."

lines: prabhu kahe—eta anna khāite nā pāri
devanagari: भोजन करह, छाड़ वचन - चातुरी ।
प्रभु कहे - एत अन्न खाइते ना पारि ॥72॥
cc-madhya-3.72.translation: Advaita Ācārya thus requested Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu to eat and give up juggling words. The Lord replied, "I certainly cannot eat so much food."

lines: yadi khāite nā pāra pāte rahibeka āra
devanagari: आचार्य बले - अकपटे करह आहार ।
यदि खाइते ना पार पाते रहिबेक आर ॥73॥
cc-madhya-3.73.translation: Advaita Ācārya then requested the Lord to simply accept the prasāda without pretense. If He could not eat it all, the balance could be left on the plate.

devanagari: प्रभु बले - एत अन्न नारिब खाइते ।
सन्न्यासीर धर्म नहे उच्छिष्ट राखिते ॥74॥
cc-madhya-3.74.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "I will not be able to eat so much food, and it is not the duty of a sannyāsī to leave remnants."

lines: eka-bāre anna khāo śata śata bhāra
devanagari: आचार्य बले - नीलाचले खाओ चौयान्न - बार ।
एक - बारे अन्न खाओ शत शत भार ॥75॥
cc-madhya-3.75.translation: In this connection Advaita Ācārya referred to Caitanya Mahāprabhu's eating at Jagannātha Purī. Lord Jagannātha and Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu are identical. Advaita Ācārya pointed out that at Jagannātha Purī Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate fifty-four times, and each time He ate many hundreds of pots of food.

lines: tāra lekhāya ei anna nahe pañca-grāsa
devanagari: तिन जनार भक्ष्य - पिण्ड - तोमार एक ग्रास ।
तार लेखाय एई अन्न नहे पञ्च - ग्रास ॥76॥
cc-madhya-3.76.translation: Śrī Advaita Ācārya said, "The amount of food that three people can eat does not constitute even a morsel for You. In proportion to that, these edibles are not even five morsels of food for You."

lines: mora bhāgye, mora ghare, tomāra āgamana
devanagari: मोर भाग्ये, मोर घरे, तोमार आगमन ।
छाड़ह चातुरी, प्रभु, करह भोजन ॥77॥
cc-madhya-3.77.translation: Advaita Ācārya continued, "By My great fortune You have just come to My home. Please do not juggle words. Just begin eating and do not talk."

lines: eta bali' jala dila dui gosāñira hāte
devanagari: एत ब लि’ जल दिल दुइ गोसाञि र हाते ।
हासिया लागला दुँहे भोजन करते ॥78॥
cc-madhya-3.78.translation: Upon saying this, Advaita Ācārya supplied water to the two Lords so that They could wash Their hands. The two Lords then sat down and, smiling, began to eat the prasāda.

lines: āji pāraṇā karite chila baḍa āśa
devanagari: नित्यानन्द कहे - कैलुँ तिन उपवास ।
आजि पारणा करिते छिल बड़ आश ॥79॥
cc-madhya-3.79.translation: Nityānanda Prabhu said, "I have undergone fasting for three days continuously. Today I hoped to break My fast."

devanagari: परात्म - निष्ठा - मात्र वेष - धारण ।
मुकुन्द - सेवाय हय संसार - तारण ॥8॥
cc-madhya-3.8.translation: The real purpose of accepting sannyāsa is to dedicate oneself to the service of Mukunda. By serving Mukunda, one can actually be liberated from the bondage of material existence.

lines: ardha-peṭa nā bharibe ei grāseka anne
devanagari: आजि उपवास हैल आचार्य - निमन्त्रणे ।
अर्ध - पेट ना भरिबे एइ ग्रासेक अन्ने ॥80॥
cc-madhya-3.80.translation: Although Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu was thinking that the quantity of food was enormous, Nityānanda Prabhu, on the contrary, thought it not even a morsel. He had been fasting for three days and had greatly hoped to break fast on that day. Indeed, He said, "Although I am invited to eat by Advaita Ācārya, today also is a fast. So small a quantity of foodstuffs will not even fill half My belly."

devanagari: आचार्य कहे - तुमि हओ तैर्थिक सन्न्यासी ।
कभु फल - मूल खाओ, कभु उपवासी ॥81॥
cc-madhya-3.81.translation: Advaita Ācārya replied, "Sir, You are a mendicant traveling on pilgrimages. Sometimes You eat fruits and roots, and sometimes You simply go on fasting.

devanagari: दरिद्र - ब्राह्मण - घरे ये पाइला मुष्ट्येक अन्न ।
इहाते सन्तुष्ट हओ, छाड़ लोभ - मन ॥82॥
cc-madhya-3.82.translation: "I am a poor brāhmaṇa, and You have come to My home. Please be satisfied with whatever little foodstuffs You have received and give up Your greedy mentality."

lines: tata dite cāha, yata kariye bhojana
devanagari: नित्या नन्द बले - यबे कैले निमन्त्रण ।
तत दिते चाह, यत करिये भोजन ॥83॥
cc-madhya-3.83.translation: Lord Nityānanda Prabhu replied, "Whatever I may be, You have invited Me. Therefore You must supply as much as I want to eat."

devanagari: शुनि’ नित्यानन्देर कथा ठाकुर अद्वैत ।
कहेन ताँहारे किछु पाइया पिरीत ॥84॥
cc-madhya-3.84.translation: His Divine Grace Advaita Ācārya, after hearing the statement of Nityānanda Prabhu, took the opportunity presented by the joking words and spoke to Him as follows.

devanagari: भ्रष्ट अवधूत तुमि, उदर भरिते ।
सन्न्या स लइयाछ, बुझि, ब्राह्मण दण्डिते ॥85॥
cc-madhya-3.85.translation: Advaita Ācārya said, "You are a reject paramahaṁsa, and You have accepted the renounced order of life just to fill up Your belly. I can understand that Your business is to give trouble to brāhmaṇas."

lines: tumi khete pāra daśa-viśa mānera anna
āmi tāhā kāṅhā pāba daridra brāhmaṇa
devanagari: तुमि खेते पार दश - विश मानेर अन्न ।
आमि ताहा काँहा पाब दरिद्र ब्राह्मण ॥86॥
cc-madhya-3.86.translation: Advaita Ācārya accused Nityānanda Prabhu, saying, "You can eat ten to twenty mānas of rice. I am a poor brāhmaṇa. How shall I get so much rice?

lines: ye pāñācha muṣṭy-eka anna, tāhā khāñā uṭha
pāgalāmi nā kariha, nā chaḍāio jhuṭha
devanagari: ये पाञाछ मुष्ट्येक अन्न, ताहा खाञा उठ ।
पागलामि ना करिह, ना छड़ाइओ झुठ ॥87॥
cc-madhya-3.87.translation: "Whatever You have, though it be a palmful of rice, please eat it and get up. Don't show Your madness and strew the remnants of food here and there."

devanagari: एइ मत हास्य - रसे करेन भोजन ।
अर्ध - अर्ध खाञा प्रभु छाड़ेन व्यञ्जन ॥88॥
cc-madhya-3.88.translation: In this way, Nityānanda Prabhu and Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu ate and talked with Advaita Ācārya jokingly. After eating half of each vegetable preparation given to Him, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu abandoned it and went on to the next.

lines: sei vyañjana ācārya punaḥ karena pūraṇa
ei mata punaḥ punaḥ pariveśe vyañjana
devanagari: सेइ व्यञ्जन आचार्य पुनः करेन पूरण ।
एइ मत पुनः पुनः परिवेशे व्यञ्जन ॥89॥
cc-madhya-3.89.translation: As soon as half of the vegetable in the pot was finished, Advaita Ācārya filled it up again. In this way, as the Lord finished half of a preparation, Advaita Ācārya again and again filled it up.

lines: sei veṣa kaila, ebe vṛndāvana giyā
devanagari: सेइ वेष कैल, एबे वृन्दावन गिया ।
कृष्ण - निषेवण करि निभृते वसिया ॥9॥
cc-madhya-3.9.translation: After accepting the sannyāsa order, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu decided to go to Vṛndāvana and engage Himself wholly and solely in the service of Mukunda in a solitary place.

devanagari: दोना व्यञ्जने भ रि’ करेन प्रार्थन ।
प्रभु बलेन - आर कत करिब भोजन ॥90॥
cc-madhya-3.90.translation: After filling a pot with vegetables, Advaita Ācārya requested Them to eat more, and Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "How much more can I go on eating?"

lines: ācārya kahe—ye diyāchi, tāhā nā chāḍibā
ekhana ye diye, tāra ardheka khāibā
devanagari: आचार्य कहे - ये दियाछि, ताहा ना छाड़िबा ।
एखन ये दिये, तार अर्धक खाइबा ॥91॥
cc-madhya-3.91.translation: Advaita Ācārya said, "Please do not give up whatever I have already given You. Now, whatever I am giving, You may eat half and leave half."

devanagari: नाना यत्न - दैन्ये प्रभुरे कराइल भोजन ।
आचा र्येर इच्छा प्रभु करिल पूरण ॥92॥
cc-madhya-3.92.translation: In this way, by submitting various humble requests, Advaita Ācārya made Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and Lord Nityānanda eat. Thus Caitanya Mahāprabhu fulfilled all the desires of Advaita Ācārya.

lines: lañā yāha, tora anna kichu nā khāila
devanagari: नित्यानन्द कहे - आमार पेट ना भरिल ।
लञा याह, तोर अन्न किछु ना खाइल ॥93॥
cc-madhya-3.93.translation: Again Nityānanda Prabhu jokingly said, "My belly is not yet filled up. Please take away Your foodstuff. I have not taken the least of it."

lines: eta bali' eka-grāsa bhāta hāte lañā
ujhāli' phelila āge yena kruddha hañā
devanagari: एत ब लि’ एक - ग्रास भात हाते लञा ।
उझालि’ फेलिल आगे येन क्रुद्ध हञा ॥94॥
cc-madhya-3.94.translation: After saying this, Nityānanda Prabhu took a handful of rice and threw it on the floor in front of Him, as if He were angry.

lines: bhāta aṅge lañā ācārya nāce bahu-raṅge
devanagari: भात दुइ - चारि लागे आचार्येर अङ्गे ।
भात अड़े लञा आचार्य नाचे बहु - रङ्गे ॥95॥
cc-madhya-3.95.translation: When two or four pieces of the thrown rice touched His body, Advaita Ācārya began to dance in various ways with the rice still stuck to His body.

lines: parama pavitra more kaila ei ḍhaṅge
devanagari: अवधूतेर झुठा लागिल मोर अङ्गे ।
परम पवित्र मोरे कैल एइ ढङ्गे ॥96॥
cc-madhya-3.96.translation: When the rice thrown by Nityānanda Prabhu touched His body, Advaita Ācārya thought Himself purified by the touch of remnants thrown by Paramahaṁsa Nityānanda. Therefore He began dancing.

lines: tore nimantraṇa kari' pāinu tāra phala
devanagari: तोरे निमन्त्रण क रि’ पाइनु तार फल ।
तोर जाति - कुल नाहि, सहजे पागल ॥97॥
cc-madhya-3.97.translation: Advaita Ācārya jokingly said, "My dear Nityānanda, I invited You, and indeed I have received the results. You have no fixed caste or dynasty. By nature You are a madman.

lines: jhuṭhā dile, vipra bali' bhaya nā karile
devanagari: आपनार सम मोरे करिबार तरे ।
झुठा दिले, विप्र ब लि’ भय ना करिले ॥98॥
cc-madhya-3.98.translation: "To make Me a madman like Yourself, You have thrown the remnants of Your food at Me. You did not even fear the fact that I am a brāhmaṇa."

devanagari: नित्यानन्द बले , - एइ कृष्णेर प्रसाद ।
इहाके ‘झुठा’ कहिले, तुमि कैले अपराध ॥99॥
cc-madhya-3.99.translation: Nityānanda Prabhu replied, "These are the remnants of food left by Lord Kṛṣṇa. If You take them to be ordinary remnants, You have committed an offense."

devanagari: यस्मै दातुं चोरयन्क्षीर - भाण्डं गोपीनाथः क्षीर - चोराभिधोऽभूत् ।
श्री - गोपालः प्रादुरासीद्वशः सन् यत्प्रेम्णा तं माधवेन्द्रं नतोऽस्मि ॥1॥
cc-madhya-4.1.translation: I offer my respectful obeisances unto Mādhavendra Purī, who was given a pot of sweet rice stolen by Śrī Gopīnātha, celebrated thereafter as Kṣīra-corā. Being pleased by Mādhavendra Purī's love, Śrī Gopāla, the Deity at Govardhana, appeared to the public vision.

devanagari: एइ - मत महाप्रभु चलिला नीलाचले ।
चारि भक्त सङ्गे कृष्ण - कीर्तन - कुतूहले ॥10॥
cc-madhya-4.10.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu proceeded toward Jagannātha Purī with four of His devotees, and He chanted the holy name of the Lord, the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, with great eagerness.

devanagari: स्वर्ण, रौप्य, वस्त्र, गन्ध, भक्ष्य - उपहार ।
असङ्ख्य आइसे, नित्य बाड़िल भाण्डार ॥100॥
cc-madhya-4.100.translation: Thus countless presentations of gold, silver, garments, scented articles and eatables arrived. The store of Gopāla increased daily.

lines: keha pāka-bhāṇḍāra kaila, keha ta' prācīra
devanagari: एक महा - धनी क्षत्रिय कराइल मन्दिर ।
केह पाक - भाण्डार कैल, केह त’ प्राचीर ॥101॥
cc-madhya-4.101.translation: One very rich kṣatriya of the royal order constructed a temple, someone made cooking utensils, and someone constructed boundary walls.

lines: eka eka vraja-vāsī eka eka gābhī dila
devanagari: एक एक व्रज - वासी एक एक गाभी दिल ।
सहस्र सहस्र गाभी गोपालेर हैल ॥102॥
cc-madhya-4.102.translation: Each and every family residing in the land of Vrajabhūmi contributed one cow. In this way, thousands of cows became the property of Gopāla.

lines: gauḍa ha-ite āilā dui vairāgī brāhmaṇa
devanagari: गौड़ हइते आइला दुइ वैरागी ब्राह्मण ।
पुरी - गोसाञि राखिल तारे करिया यतन ॥103॥
cc-madhya-4.103.translation: Eventually two brāhmaṇas in the renounced order arrived from Bengal, and Mādhavendra Purī, who liked them very much, kept them in Vṛndāvana and gave them all kinds of comforts.

lines: sei dui śiṣya kari' sevā samarpila
devanagari: सेइ दुइ शिष्य करि’ सेवा समर्पिल ।
राज - सेवा हय , - पुरीर आनन्द बाड़िल ॥104॥
cc-madhya-4.104.translation: These two were then initiated by Mādhavendra Purī, and he entrusted them with the daily service of the Lord. This service was performed continuously, and the worship of the Deity became very gorgeous. Thus Mādhavendra Purī was very pleased.

devanagari: एइ - मत वत्सर दुइ करिल सेवन ।
एक - दिन पुरी - गोसाञि देखिल स्वपन ॥105॥
cc-madhya-4.105.translation: In this way the Deity worship in the temple was very gorgeously performed for two years. Then one day Mādhavendra Purī had a dream.

lines: gopāla kahe, purī āmāra tāpa nāhi yāya
devanagari: गोपाल कहे, पुरी आमार ताप नाहि याय ।
मलयज - चन्दन ले प’, तबे से जुड़ाय ॥106॥
cc-madhya-4.106.translation: In his dream, Mādhavendra Purī saw Gopāla, who said, "My bodily temperature still has not decreased. Please bring sandalwood from the Malaya province and smear the pulp over My body to cool Me.

lines: anye haite nahe, tumi calaha tvarite
devanagari: मलयज आन, याञा नीलाचल हैते ।
अन्ये हैते नहे, तुमि चलह त्वरिते ॥107॥
cc-madhya-4.107.translation: "Bring sandalwood pulp from Jagannātha Purī. Kindly go quickly. Since no one else can do it, you must."

devanagari: स्वप्न देखि’ पुरी - गोसाञि र हैल प्रेमावेश ।
प्रभु - आज्ञा पालिबारे गेला पूर्व - देश ॥108॥
cc-madhya-4.108.translation: After having this dream, Mādhavendra Purī Gosvāmī became very glad due to ecstasy of love of Godhead, and in order to execute the command of the Lord, he started east toward Bengal.

devanagari: सेवार निर्बन्ध - लोक करिल स्थापन ।
आज्ञा मा गि’ गौड़ - देशे करिल गमन ॥109॥
cc-madhya-4.109.translation: Before leaving, Mādhavendra Purī made all arrangements for regular Deity worship, and he engaged different people in various duties. Then, taking up the order of Gopāla, he started for Bengal.

lines: bhikṣā lāgi' eka-dina eka grāma giyā
devanagari: भिक्षा ला गि’ एक - दिन एक ग्राम गिया ।
आपने बहुत अन्न आनिल मागिया ॥11॥
cc-madhya-4.11.translation: Each day Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally went to a village and collected a great quantity of rice and other grains for the preparation of prasāda.

lines: purīra prema dekhi' ācārya ānanda antare
devanagari: शान्तिपुर आइला अद्वैताचार्येर घरे ।
पुरीर प्रेम देखि’ आचार्य आनन्द अन्तरे ॥110॥
cc-madhya-4.110.translation: When Mādhavendra Purī arrived at the house of Advaita Ācārya in Śāntipura, the Ācārya became very pleased upon seeing the ecstatic love of Godhead manifest in Mādhavendra Purī.

lines: tāṅra ṭhāñi mantra laila yatana kariñā
calilā dakṣiṇe purī tāṅre dīkṣā diñā
devanagari: ताँर ठाञि मन्त्र लैल ऋतन करिञा ।
चलिला दक्षिणे पुरी ताँरे दीक्षा दिला ॥111॥
cc-madhya-4.111.translation: Advaita Ācārya begged to be initiated by Mādhavendra Purī. After initiating Him, Mādhavendra Purī started for South India.

devanagari: रेमुणाते कैल गोपीनाथ दरशन ।
ताँर रूप देखिला हैल विह्वल - मन ॥112॥
cc-madhya-4.112.translation: Going into South India, Śrī Mādhavendra Purī visited Remuṇā, where Gopīnātha is situated. Upon seeing the beauty of the Deity, Mādhavendra Purī was overwhelmed.

devanagari: नृत्य - गीत क रि’ जग - मोहने वसिला ।
‘क्या क्या भोग लागे ?’ ब्राह्मणे पुछिला ॥113॥
cc-madhya-4.113.translation: In the corridor of the temple, from which people generally viewed the Deity, Mādhavendra Purī chanted and danced. Then he sat down there and asked a brāhmaṇa what kinds of foods they offered to the Deity.

devanagari: सेवार सौष्ठव देखि’ आनन्दित मने ।
उत्तम भोग लागे - एथा बुझि अनुमाने ॥114॥
cc-madhya-4.114.translation: From the excellence of the arrangements, Mādhavendra Purī understood by deduction that only the best food was offered.

lines: yaiche ihā bhoga lāge, sakala-i puchiba
devanagari: यैछे इहा भोग लागे, सकल - इ पुछिब ।
तैछे भियाने भोग गोपाले लागाइब ॥115॥
cc-madhya-4.115.translation: Mādhavendra Purī thought, "I shall inquire from the priest what foods are offered to Gopīnātha so that by making arrangements in our kitchen, we can offer similar foods to Śrī Gopāla."

devanagari: एइ ला गि’ पुछिलेन ब्राह्मणेर स्थाने ।
ब्राह्मण कहिल सब भोग - विवरणे ॥116॥
cc-madhya-4.116.translation: When the brāhmaṇa priest was questioned in this matter, he explained in detail what kinds of foods were offered to the Deity of Gopīnātha.

devanagari: सन्ध्याय भोग लागे क्षीर - ‘अमृत - केलि’ नाम ।
द्वादश मृत्पात्रे भरि’ अमृत - समान ॥117॥
cc-madhya-4.117.translation: The brāhmaṇa priest said, "In the evening the Deity is offered sweet rice in twelve earthen pots. Because the taste is as good as nectar [amṛta], it is named amṛta-keli.

lines: pṛthivīte aiche bhoga kāhāṅ nāhi āra
devanagari: ‘गोपीनाथेर क्षी र’ बलि’ प्रसिद्ध नाम यार ।
पृथिवीते ऐछे भोग काहाँ नाहि आर ॥118॥
cc-madhya-4.118.translation: "This sweet rice is celebrated throughout the world as gopīnātha-kṣīra. It is not offered anywhere else in the world."

devanagari: हेन - काले सेइ भोग ठाकुरे लागिल ।
शुनि’ पुरी - गोसाञि किछु मने विचारिल ॥119॥
cc-madhya-4.119.translation: While Mādhavendra Purī was talking with the brāhmaṇa priest, the sweet rice was placed before the Deity as an offering. Hearing this, Mādhavendra Purī thought as follows.

lines: pathe baḍa baḍa dānī vighna nāhi kare
tā' sabāre kṛpā kari' āilā remuṇāre
devanagari: पथे बड़ बड़ दानी विघ्न नाहि करे ।
ता’ सबारे कृपा करि’ आइला रे मुणारे ॥12॥
cc-madhya-4.12.translation: There were many rivers on the way, and at each river there was a tax collector. They did not hinder the Lord, however, and He showed them mercy. Finally He reached the village of Remuṇā.

lines: ayācita kṣīra prasāda alpa yadi pāi
svāda jāni' taiche kṣīra gopāle lāgāi
devanagari: अयाचित क्षीर प्रसाद अल्प यदि पाइ ।
स्वाद जा नि’ तैछे क्षीर गोपाले लागाइ ॥120॥
cc-madhya-4.120.translation: "If, without my asking, a little sweet rice is given to me, I can then taste it and make a similar preparation to offer my Lord Gopāla."

lines: ei icchāya lajjā pāñā viṣṇu-smaraṇa kaila
devanagari: एइ इच्छाय लज्जा पाञा विष्णु - स्मरण कैल ।
हेन - काले भोग स रि’ आरति बाजिल ॥121॥
cc-madhya-4.121.translation: Mādhavendra Purī became greatly ashamed when he desired to taste the sweet rice, and he immediately began to think of Lord Viṣṇu. While he was thus thinking of Lord Viṣṇu, the offering was completed, and the ārati ceremony began.

lines: bāhire āilā, kāre kichu nā kahila āra
devanagari: आरति देखिया पुरी कैल नमस्कार ।
बाहिरे आइला, कारे किछु ना कहिल आर ॥122॥
cc-madhya-4.122.translation: After the ārati was finished, Mādhavendra Purī offered his obeisances to the Deity and then left the temple. He did not say anything more to anyone.

devanagari: अयाचित - वृत्ति पुरी - विरक्त, उदास ।
अयाचित पाइले खा’न, नहे उपवास ॥123॥
cc-madhya-4.123.translation: Mādhavendra Purī avoided begging. He was completely unattached and indifferent to material things. He would not beg. If someone offered him some food, he would eat; otherwise he would fast.

devanagari: प्रेमामृते तृप्त, क्षुधा - तृष्णा नाहि बाधे ।
क्षीर - इच्छा हैल, ताहे माने अपराधे ॥124॥
cc-madhya-4.124.translation: A paramahaṁsa like Mādhavendra Purī is always satisfied in the loving service of the Lord. Material hunger and thirst cannot impede his activities. When he desired to taste a little sweet rice offered to the Deity, he considered that he had committed an offense by desiring to eat what was being offered to the Deity.

devanagari: ग्रामेर शून्य - हाटे व सि’ करेन कीर्तन ।
एथा पूजारी कराइल ठाकुरे शयन ॥125॥
cc-madhya-4.125.translation: Mādhavendra Purī left the temple and sat down in the village marketplace, which was vacant. Sitting there, he began to chant. In the meantime, the temple priest laid the Deity down to rest.

lines: nija kṛtya kari' pūjārī karila śayana
devanagari: निज कृत्य करि’ पूजारी करिल शयन ।
स्वपने ठाकुर आसि’ बलिला वचन ॥126॥
cc-madhya-4.126.translation: Finishing his daily duties, the priest went to take rest. In a dream he saw the Gopīnātha Deity come to talk to him, and He spoke as follows.

devanagari: उठह, पूजारी, कर द्वार विमोचन ।
क्षीर एक राखियाछि सन्न्यासि - कारण ॥127॥
cc-madhya-4.127.translation: "Please get up and open the door of the temple. I have kept one pot of sweet rice for the sannyāsī Mādhavendra Purī.

lines: dhaḍāra añcale ḍhākā eka kṣīra haya
tomarā nā jānilā tāhā āmāra māyāya
devanagari: धड़ार अञ्चले ढाका एक क्षीर हय ।
तोमरा ना जानिला ताहा आमार मायाय ॥128॥
cc-madhya-4.128.translation: "This pot of sweet rice is just behind My cloth curtain. You did not see it because of My tricks.

lines: tāhāke ta' ei kṣīra śīghra deha lañā
devanagari: माधव - पुरी सन्न्यासी आछे हाटेते वसिञा ।
ताहाके त’ एइ क्षीर शीघ्र देह लञा ॥129॥
cc-madhya-4.129.translation: "A sannyāsī named Mādhavendra Purī is sitting in the vacant marketplace. Please take this pot of sweet rice from behind Me and deliver it to him."

lines: bhakti kari' kaila prabhu tāṅra daraśana
devanagari: रेमुणाते गोपीनाथ परम - मोहन ।
भक्ति क रि’ कैल प्रभु ताँर दरशन ॥13॥
cc-madhya-4.13.translation: The Deity of Gopīnātha in the temple at Remuṇā was very attractive. Lord Caitanya visited the temple and offered His obeisances with great devotion.

lines: svapna dekhi' pūjārī uṭhi' karilā vicāra
snāna kari' kapāṭa khuli, mukta kaila dvāra
devanagari: स्वप्न देखि’ पूजारी उठि’ करिला विचार ।
स्नान क रि’ कपाट खुलि, मुक्त कैल द्वार ॥130॥
cc-madhya-4.130.translation: Awaking from the dream, the priest immediately rose from bed and thought it wise to take a bath before entering the Deity's room. He then opened the temple door.

lines: sthāna lepi' kṣīra lañā ha-ila bāhira
devanagari: धड़ार आँचल - तले पाइल सेइ क्षीर ।
स्थान ले पि’ क्षीर लञा हइल बाहिर ॥131॥
cc-madhya-4.131.translation: According to the Deity's directions, the priest found the pot of sweet rice behind the cloth curtain. He removed the pot and mopped up the place where it had been kept. He then went out of the temple.

lines: dvāra diyā grāme gelā sei kṣīra lañā
devanagari: द्वार दिया ग्रामे गेला सेइ क्षीर लञा ।
हाटे हाटे बुले माधव - पुरीके चाहिञा ॥132॥
cc-madhya-4.132.translation: Closing the door of the temple, he went to the village with the pot of sweet rice. He called out in every stall in search of Mādhavendra Purī.

lines: tomā lāgi' gopīnātha kṣīra kaila curi
devanagari: क्षीर लह एइ, यार नाम ‘माधव - पुरी’ ।
तोमा ला गि’ गोपीनाथ क्षीर कैल चुरि ॥133॥
cc-madhya-4.133.translation: Holding the pot of sweet rice, the priest called, "Will he whose name is Mādhavendra Purī please come and take this pot! Gopīnātha has stolen this pot for you!"

lines: kṣīra lañā sukhe tumi karaha bhakṣaṇe
devanagari: क्षीर लञा सुखे तुमि करह भक्षणे ।
तोमा - सम भाग्यतान् नाहि त्रिभुवने ॥134॥
cc-madhya-4.134.translation: The priest continued, "Would the sannyāsī whose name is Mādhavendra Purī please come and take this pot of sweet rice and enjoy the prasāda with great happiness! You are the most fortunate person within these three worlds!"

lines: kṣīra diyā pūjārī tāṅre daṇḍavat haila
devanagari: एत शुनि’ पुरी - गोसाञि परिचय दिल ।
क्षीर दिया पूजारी ताँरे दण्डवत् हैल ॥135॥
cc-madhya-4.135.translation: Hearing this invitation, Mādhavendra Purī came out and identified himself. The priest then delivered the pot of sweet rice and offered his obeisances, falling flat before him.

devanagari: क्षीरेर वृत्तान्त ताँरे कहिल पूजारी ।
शुनि’ प्रेमाविष्ट हैल श्री - माधव - पुरी ॥136॥
cc-madhya-4.136.translation: When the story about the pot of sweet rice was explained to him in detail, Śrī Mādhavendra Purī at once became absorbed in ecstatic love of Kṛṣṇa.

lines: prema dekhi' sevaka kahe ha-iyā vismita
devanagari: प्रेम देखि’ सेवक कहे हइया विस्मित ।
कृष्ण ने इँहार वश, - हय यथोचित ॥137॥
cc-madhya-4.137.translation: Upon seeing the ecstatic loving symptoms manifest in Mādhavendra Purī, the priest was struck with wonder. He could understand why Kṛṣṇa had become so much obliged to him, and he saw that Kṛṣṇa's action was befitting.

lines: āveśe karilā purī se kṣīra bhakṣaṇa
devanagari: एत ब लि’ नमस्क रि’ करिला गमन ।
आवेशे करिला पुरी से क्षीर भक्षण ॥138॥
cc-madhya-4.138.translation: The priest offered his obeisances to Mādhavendra Purī and returned to the temple. Then, in ecstasy, Mādhavendra Purī ate the sweet rice offered to him by Kṛṣṇa.

lines: pātra prakṣālana kari' khaṇḍa khaṇḍa kaila
devanagari: पात्र प्रक्षालन क रि’ खण्ड खण्ड कैल ।
बहिर्वासे बा न्धि’ सेइ ठिकारि राखिल ॥139॥
cc-madhya-4.139.translation: After this, Mādhavendra Purī washed the pot and broke it into pieces. He then bound all the pieces in his outer cloth and kept them nicely.

devanagari: ताँर पाद - पद्म निकट प्रणाम करिते ।
ताँर पुष्प - चूड़ा पड़िल प्रभुर माथाते ॥14॥
cc-madhya-4.14.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu offered His obeisances at the lotus feet of the Gopīnātha Deity, the helmet of flowers on the head of Gopīnātha fell down and landed on the head of Caitanya Mahāprabhu.

devanagari: प्रति - दिन एक - खानि करेन भक्षण ।
खाइले प्रेमावेश हय , - अद्भुत कथन ॥140॥
cc-madhya-4.140.translation: Each day, Mādhavendra Purī would eat one piece of that earthen pot, and after eating it he would immediately be overwhelmed with ecstasy. These are wonderful stories.

lines: dine loka-bhiḍa habe mora pratiṣṭhā jāni'
devanagari: ‘ठाकुर मोरे क्षीर दिल - लोक सब श नि’ ।
दिने लोक - भिड़ हबे मोर प्रतिष्ठा जा नि’ ॥141॥
cc-madhya-4.141.translation: Having broken the pot and bound the pieces in his cloth, Mādhavendra Purī began to think, "The Lord has given me a pot of sweet rice, and when the people hear of this tomorrow morning, there will be great crowds."

devanagari: सेइ भये रात्रि - शेषे चलिला श्री - पुरी ।
सेइ - खाने गोपीनाथे दण्डवत्क रि’ ॥142॥
cc-madhya-4.142.translation: Thinking this, Śrī Mādhavendra Purī offered his obeisances to Gopīnātha on the spot and left Remuṇā before morning.

devanagari: चलि’ चलि’ आइला पुरी श्री - नीलाचल ।
जगन्नाथ देखि’ हैला प्रेमेते विह्वल ॥143॥
cc-madhya-4.143.translation: Walking and walking, Mādhavendra Purī finally reached Jagannātha Purī, which is also known as Nīlācala. There he saw Lord Jagannātha and was overwhelmed with loving ecstasy.

lines: premāveśe uṭhe, paḍe, hāse, nāce, gāya
devanagari: प्रेमावेशे उठे, पड़े, हासे, नाचे, गाय ।
जगन्नाथ - दरशने महा - सुख पाय ॥144॥
cc-madhya-4.144.translation: When Mādhavendra Purī was overwhelmed in the ecstasy of love of Godhead, he sometimes stood up and sometimes fell to the ground. Sometimes he laughed, danced and sang. In this way he enjoyed transcendental bliss by seeing the Jagannātha Deity.

lines: saba loka āsi' tāṅre kare bahu bhakti
devanagari: ‘माधव - पुरी श्रीपाद आइल’, - लोके हैल ख्याति ।
सब लोक आ सि’ ताँरे करे बहु भक्ति ॥145॥
cc-madhya-4.145.translation: When Mādhavendra Purī came to Jagannātha Purī, people were aware of his transcendental reputation. Therefore crowds of people came and offered him all sorts of respect in devotion.

lines: ye nā vāñche, tāra haya vidhātā-nirmita
devanagari: प्रतिष्ठार स्वभाव एइ जगते विदित ।
ये ना वाञ्छे, तार हय विधाता - निर्मित ॥146॥
cc-madhya-4.146.translation: Even though one may not like it, reputation, as ordained by providence, comes to him. Indeed, one's transcendental reputation is known throughout the entire world.

devanagari: प्रतिष्ठार भये पुरी गेला पलाञा ।
कृष्ण - प्रेमे प्रतिष्ठा चले सङ्गे गड़ाञा ॥147॥
cc-madhya-4.147.translation: Being afraid of his reputation [pratiṣṭhā], Mādhavendra Purī fled from Remuṇā. But the reputation brought by love of Godhead is so sublime that it goes along with the devotee, as if following him.

devanagari: यद्यपि उद्वेग हैल पलाइते मन ।
ठाकुरेर चन्दन - साधन हुइल बन्धन ॥148॥
cc-madhya-4.148.translation: Mādhavendra Purī wanted to leave Jagannātha Purī because the people were honoring him as a great devotee; however, this threatened to hinder his collecting sandalwood for the Gopāla Deity.

devanagari: जगन्नाथेर सेवक यत, यतेक महान्त ।
सबाके कहिल पुरी गोपाल - वृत्तान्त ॥149॥
cc-madhya-4.149.translation: Śrī Mādhavendra Purī told all the servants of Lord Jagannātha and all the great devotees there the story of the appearance of Śrī Gopāla.

devanagari: चूड़ा पाञा महाप्रभुर आनन्दित मन ।
बहु नृत्य - गीत कैल लञा भक्त - गण ॥15॥
cc-madhya-4.15.translation: When the Deity's helmet fell upon His head, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu became very pleased, and thus He chanted and danced in various ways with His devotees.

devanagari: गोपाल चन्दन मागे , - शुनि’ भक्त - गण ।
आनन्दे चन्दन ला गि’ करिल यतन ॥150॥
cc-madhya-4.150.translation: When all the devotees at Jagannātha Purī heard that the Gopāla Deity wanted sandalwood, in great pleasure they all endeavored to collect it.

devanagari: राज - पात्र - सने यार यार परिचय ।
तारे मा गि’ कर्पूर - चन्दन करिला सञ्चय ॥151॥
cc-madhya-4.151.translation: Those who were acquainted with government officers met with them and begged for camphor and sandalwood, which they collected.

lines: eka vipra, eka sevaka, candana vahite
devanagari: एक विप्र, एक सेवक, चन्दन वहिते ।
पुरी - गोसाञि र सङ्गे दिल सम्बल - सहिते ॥152॥
cc-madhya-4.152.translation: One brāhmaṇa and one servant were given to Mādhavendra Purī just to carry the sandalwood. He was also given the necessary traveling expenses.

devanagari: घाटी - दानी छाड़ाइते राज - पात्र द्वारे ।
राज - लेखा क रि’ दिल पुरी - गोसाञि र करे ॥153॥
cc-madhya-4.153.translation: To get past the toll collectors along the way, Mādhavendra Purī was supplied with the necessary release papers from government officers. The papers were placed in his hand.

devanagari: चलिल माधव - पुरी चन्दन लञा ।
कत - दिने रेणाते उत्तरिल गिया ॥154॥
cc-madhya-4.154.translation: In this way Mādhavendra Purī started for Vṛndāvana with the burden of sandalwood, and after some days he again reached the village of Remuṇā and the Gopīnātha temple there.

devanagari: गोपीनाथ - चरणे कैल बहु नमस्कार ।
प्रेमावेशे नृत्य - गीत करिला अपार ॥155॥
cc-madhya-4.155.translation: When Mādhavendra Purī reached the temple of Gopīnātha, he offered his respectful obeisances many times at the lotus feet of the Lord. In the ecstasy of love, he began to dance and sing without cessation.

lines: purī dekhi' sevaka saba sammāna karila
devanagari: पुरी देखि’ सेवक सब सम्मान करिल ।
क्षीर - प्रसाद दिया ताँरे भिक्षा कराइल ॥156॥
cc-madhya-4.156.translation: When the priest of Gopīnātha saw Mādhavendra Purī again, he offered all respects to him and, giving him the sweet rice prasāda, made him eat.

devanagari: सेइ रात्रे देवालये करिल शयन ।
शेष - रात्रि हैले पुरी देखिल स्वपन ॥157॥
cc-madhya-4.157.translation: Mādhavendra Purī took rest that night in the temple, but toward the end of the night he had another dream.

devanagari: गोपाल आसिया कहे , - शुन हे माधव ।
कर्पूर - चन्दन आमि पाइलाम सब ॥158॥
cc-madhya-4.158.translation: Mādhavendra Purī dreamed that Gopāla came before him and said, "O Mādhavendra Purī, I have already received all the sandalwood and camphor.

devanagari: कर्पूर - सहित घषि’ ए - सब चन्दन ।
गोपीनाथेर अङ्गे नित्य करह लेपन ॥159॥
cc-madhya-4.159.translation: "Now just grind all the sandalwood together with the camphor and then smear the pulp on the body of Gopīnātha daily until it is finished.

devanagari: प्रभुर प्रभाव देखि’ प्रेम - रूप - गुण ।
विस्मित हइला गोपीनाथेर दास - गण ॥16॥
cc-madhya-4.16.translation: All the servants of the Deity were struck with wonder due to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's intense love, His exquisite beauty and His transcendental qualities.

lines: gopīnātha āmāra se eka-i aṅga haya
iṅhāke candana dile habe mora tāpa-kṣaya
devanagari: गोपीनाथ आमार से एक - इ अङ्ग हय ।
इँहाके चन्दन दिले हबे मोर ताप - क्षय ॥160॥
cc-madhya-4.160.translation: "There is no difference between My body and Gopīnātha's body. They are one and the same. Therefore if you smear the sandalwood pulp on the body of Gopīnātha, you will naturally also smear it on My body. Thus the temperature of My body will be reduced.

lines: dvidhā nā bhāviha, nā kariha kichu mane
viśvāsa kari' candana deha āmāra vacane
devanagari: द्विधा ना भाविह, ना करिह किछु मने ।
विश्वास क रि’ चन्दन देह आमार वचने ॥161॥
cc-madhya-4.161.translation: "You should not hesitate to act according to My order. Believing in Me, just do what is needed."

lines: eta bali' gopāla gela, gosāñi jāgilā
devanagari: एत ब लि’ गोपाल गेल, गोसाञि जागिला ।
गोपीनाथेर सेवक - गणे डाकिया आनिला ॥162॥
cc-madhya-4.162.translation: After giving these instructions, Gopāla disappeared, and Mādhavendra Purī awoke. He immediately called for all the servants of Gopīnātha, and they came before him.

devanagari: प्रभुर आज्ञा हैल, - एइ कर्पूर - चन्दन ।
गोपीनाथेर अङ्गे नित्य करह लेपन ॥163॥
cc-madhya-4.163.translation: Mādhavendra Purī said, "Smear the body of Gopīnātha with this camphor and sandalwood I have brought for Gopāla in Vṛndāvana. Do this regularly every day.

lines: iṅhāke candana dile, gopāla ha-ibe śītala
devanagari: इँहाके चन्दन दिले, गोपाल हइबे शीतल ।
स्वतन्त्र ईश्वर - ताँर आज्ञा से प्रबल ॥164॥
cc-madhya-4.164.translation: "If the sandalwood pulp is smeared over the body of Gopīnātha, then Gopāla will be cooled. After all, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is completely independent; His order is all-powerful."

devanagari: ग्रीष्म - काले गोपीनाथ परिबे चन्दन ।
शुनि’ आनन्दित हैल सेवकेर मन ॥165॥
cc-madhya-4.165.translation: The servants of Gopīnātha became very pleased to hear that in the summer all the sandalwood pulp would be used to anoint the body of Gopīnātha.

lines: āra janā-dui deha, diba ye vetana
devanagari: पुरी कहे, - एइ दुइ घषिबे चन्दन ।
आर जना - दुइ देह, दिब ये वेतन ॥166॥
cc-madhya-4.166.translation: Mādhavendra Purī said, "These two assistants will regularly grind the sandalwood, and you should also get two other people to help. I shall pay their salary."

lines: ei mata candana deya pratyaha ghaṣiyā
devanagari: एइ मत चन्दन देय प्रत्यह घषिया ।
पराय सेवक सब आनन्द करिया ॥167॥
cc-madhya-4.167.translation: In this way Gopīnāthajī was supplied ground sandalwood pulp daily. The servants of Gopīnātha were very pleased with this.

lines: pratyaha candana parāya, yāvat haila anta
devanagari: प्रत्यह चन्दन पराय, यावत् हैल अन्त ।
तथाय रहिल पुरी तावत्पर्यन्त ॥168॥
cc-madhya-4.168.translation: In this way the sandalwood pulp was smeared over the body of Gopīnātha until the whole stock was finished. Mādhavendra Purī stayed there until that time.

devanagari: ग्रीष्म - काल - अन्ते पुनः नीलाचले गेला ।
नीलाचले चातुर्मास्य आनन्दे रहिला ॥169॥
cc-madhya-4.169.translation: At the end of summer Mādhavendra Purī returned to Jagannātha Purī, where he remained with great pleasure during the whole period of Cāturmāsya.

lines: sei rātri tāhāṅ prabhu karilā vañcana
devanagari: नाना - रूपे प्रीत्ये कैल प्रभुर सेवन ।
सेइ रात्रि ताहाँ प्रभु करिला वञ्चन ॥17॥
cc-madhya-4.17.translation: Because of their love for Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they served Him in many ways, and that night the Lord stayed at the temple of Gopīnātha.

devanagari: श्री - मुखे माधव - पुरीर अमृत - चरित ।
भक्त - गणे शुनाञा प्रभु करे आस्वादित ॥170॥
cc-madhya-4.170.translation: Thus Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu personally praised the nectarean characteristics of Mādhavendra Purī, and while He related all this to the devotees, He personally relished it.

devanagari: प्रभु कहे, - नित्यानन्द, करह विचार ।
पुरी - सम भाग्यवान् जगते नाहि आर ॥171॥
cc-madhya-4.171.translation: Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu asked Nityānanda Prabhu to judge whether there was anyone within the world as fortunate as Mādhavendra Purī.

lines: tina-bāre svapne āsi' yāṅre ājñā kaila
devanagari: दुग्ध - दान - छले कृष्ण याँरे देखा दिल ।
तिन - बारे स्वप्ने आ सि’ याँरे आज्ञा कैल ॥172॥
cc-madhya-4.172.translation: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu said, "Mādhavendra Purī was so fortunate that Kṛṣṇa personally appeared before him on the plea of delivering milk. Three times the Lord gave orders to Mādhavendra Purī in dreams.

lines: yāṅra preme vaśa hañā prakaṭa ha-ilā
devanagari: याँर प्रेमे वश ह ञा प्रकट हइला ।
सेवा अङ्गीकार करि’ जगत् तारिला ॥173॥
cc-madhya-4.173.translation: "Being obliged because of the loving affairs of Mādhavendra Purī, Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself appeared as the Gopāla Deity, and, accepting his service, He liberated the whole world.

lines: yāṅra lāgi' gopīnātha kṣīra kaila curi
devanagari: याँर ला गि’ गोपीनाथ क्षीर कैल चुरि ।
अतएव नाम हैल ‘क्षीर - चोरा’ करि’ ॥174॥
cc-madhya-4.174.translation: "On account of Mādhavendra Purī, Lord Gopīnātha stole the pot of sweet rice. Thus He became famous as Kṣīra-corā [the thief who stole the sweet rice].

devanagari: कर्पूर - चन्दन याँर अङ्गे चड़ाइल ।
आनन्दे पुरी - गोसाञि र प्रेम उथलिल ॥175॥
cc-madhya-4.175.translation: "Mādhavendra Purī smeared the sandalwood pulp over the body of Gopīnātha, and in this way he was overpowered with love of Godhead.

lines: purī duḥkha pābe ihā jāniyā gopāla
devanagari: म्लेच्छ - देशे कर्पूर - चन्दन आनिते जञ्जाल ।
पुरी दुःख पाबे इहा जानिया गोपाल ॥176॥
cc-madhya-4.176.translation: "In the provinces of India governed by the Mohammedans, there was much inconvenience in traveling with sandalwood and camphor. Because of this, Mādhavendra Purī might have gotten into trouble. This became known to the Gopāla Deity.

devanagari: महा - दया - मय प्रभु - भकत - वत्सल ।
चन्दन प रि’ भक्त - श्रम करिल सफल ॥177॥
cc-madhya-4.177.translation: "The Lord is very merciful and attached to His devotees, so when Gopīnātha was covered with sandalwood pulp, Mādhavendra Purī's labor became successful."

devanagari: पुरीर प्रेम - पराकाष्ठा करह विचार ।
अलौकिक प्रेम चित्ते लागे चमत्कार ॥178॥
cc-madhya-4.178.translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu placed the standard of Mādhavendra Purī's intense love before Nityānanda Prabhu for judgment. "All his loving activities are uncommon," Caitanya Mahāprabhu said. "Indeed, one is struck with wonder to hear of his activities."

devanagari: परम विरक्त, मौनी, सर्वत्र उदासीन ।
ग्राम्य - वार्ता - भये द्वितीय - सङ्ग - हीन ॥179॥
cc-madhya-4.179.translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu continued, "Śrī Mādhavendra Purī used to remain alone. He was completely renounced and always very silent. He was uninterested in everything material, and for fear of talking about mundane things, he always lived without a companion.

devanagari: महाप्रसाद - क्षीर - लोभे रहिला प्रभु तथा ।
पूर्वे ईश्वर - पुरी ताँरे कहियाछेन कथा ॥18॥
cc-madhya-4.18.translation: The Lord remained there because He was very eager to receive the remnants of sweet rice offered to the Gopīnātha Deity, having heard a narration from His spiritual master, Īśvara Purī, of what had once happened there.

lines: sahasra krośa āsi' bule candana māgiñā
devanagari: हेन - जन गोपालेर आज्ञामृत पाञा ।
सहस्त्र क्रोश आ सि’ बुले चन्दन मागिञा ॥180॥
cc-madhya-4.180.translation: "After receiving the transcendental orders of Gopāla, this great personality traveled thousands of miles just to collect sandalwood by begging.

lines: bhoke rahe, tabu anna māgiñā nā khāya
devanagari: भोके रहे, तबु अन्न मागिञा ना खाय ।
हेन - जन चन्दन - भार व हि’ लञा याय ॥181॥
cc-madhya-4.181.translation: "Although Mādhavendra Purī was hungry, he would not beg food to eat. This renounced person carried a load of sandalwood for the sake of Śrī Gopāla.

devanagari: ‘मणेक चन्दन, तोला - विशेक कर्पूर ।
गोपाले पराइ ब’ - एइ आनन्द प्रचुर ॥182॥
cc-madhya-4.182.translation: "Without considering his personal comforts, Mādhavendra Purī carried one mound [about eighty-two pounds] of sandalwood and twenty tolās [about eight ounces] of camphor to smear over the body of Gopāla. This transcendental pleasure was sufficient for him.

devanagari: उत्कलेर दानी राखे चन्दन देखिञा ।
ताहाँ एड़ाइल राज - पत्र देखा ञा॥183॥
cc-madhya-4.183.translation: "Since there were restrictions against taking the sandalwood out of the Orissa province, the toll official confiscated the stock, but Mādhavendra Purī showed him the release papers given by the government and consequently escaped difficulties.

devanagari: म्लेच्छ - देश दूर पथ, जगाति अपार ।
के - मते चन्द न निब - नाहि ए विचार ॥184॥
cc-madhya-4.184.translation: "Mādhavendra Purī was not at all anxious during the long journey to Vṛndāvana through the provinces governed by the Mohammedans and filled with unlimited numbers of watchmen.

lines: saṅge eka vaṭa nāhi ghāṭī-dāna dite
tathāpi utsāha baḍa candana lañā yāite
devanagari: सङ्गे एक वट नाहि घाटी - दान दिते ।
तथापि उत्साह बड़ चन्दन लञा याइते ॥185॥
cc-madhya-4.185.translation: "Although Mādhavendra Purī did not have a farthing with him, he was not afraid to pass by the toll officers. His only enjoyment was in carrying the load of sandalwood to Vṛndāvana for Gopāla.

devanagari: प्रगाढ़ - प्रेमेर एइ स्वभाव - आचा र ।
निज - दुःख - विघ्नादिर ना करे विचार ॥186॥
cc-madhya-4.186.translation: "This is the natural result of intense love of Godhead. The devotee does not consider personal inconveniences or impediments. In all circumstances he wants to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

lines: ei tāra gāḍha premā loke dekhāite
gopāla tāṅre ājñā dila candana ānite
devanagari: एइ तार गाढ़ प्रेमा लोके देखाइते ।
गोपाल ताँरे आज्ञा दिल चन्दन आनिते ॥187॥
cc-madhya-4.187.translation: "Śrī Gopāla wanted to show how intensely Mādhavendra Purī loved Kṛṣṇa; therefore He asked him to go to Nīlācala to fetch sandalwood and camphor.

lines: ānanda bāḍila mane, duḥkha nā gaṇila
devanagari: बहु परिश्रमे चन्दन रेमुणा आनिल ।
आनन्द बाड़िल मने, दुःख ना गणिल ॥188॥
cc-madhya-4.188.translation: "With great trouble and after much labor, Mādhavendra Purī brought the load of sandalwood to Remuṇā. However, he was still very pleased; he discounted all the difficulties.

lines: parīkṣā karite gopāla kaila ājñā dāna
devanagari: परीक्षा करिते गोपाल कैल आज्ञा दान ।
परीक्षा करिया शेषे हैल दयावान् ॥189॥
cc-madhya-4.189.translation: "To test the intense love of Mādhavendra Purī, Gopāla, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, ordered him to bring sandalwood from Nīlācala, and when Mādhavendra Purī passed this examination, the Lord became very merciful to him.

lines: bhakta-gaṇe kahe prabhu sei ta' ākhyāna
devanagari: ‘क्षीर - चोरा गोपीनाथ’ प्रसिद्ध ताँर नाम ।
भक्त - गणे कहे प्रभु सेइ त’ आख्यान ॥19॥
cc-madhya-4.19.translation: That Deity was known widely as Kṣīra-corā-gopīnātha, and Caitanya Mahāprabhu told His devotees the story of how the Deity became so famous.

devanagari: एइ भक्ति, भक्त - प्रिय - कृष्ण - व्यवहार ।
बुझितेओ आमा - सबार नाहि अधिकार ॥190॥
cc-madhya-4.190.translation: "Such behavior exhibited in loving service between the devotee and the devotee's lovable object, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, is transcendental. It is not possible for a common man to understand. Common men do not even have the capacity."

lines: eta bali' paḍe prabhu tāṅra kṛta śloka
devanagari: एत ब लि’ पड़े प्रभु ताँर कृत श्लोक ।
येइ श्लोक - चन्द्रे जगत्कर्याछे आलोक ॥191॥
cc-madhya-4.191.translation: After saying this, Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu read the famous verse of Mādhavendra Purī. That verse is just like the moon. It has spread illumination all over the world.

lines: gandha bāḍe, taiche ei ślokera vicāra
devanagari: घषिते घषिते यैछे मलयज - सार ।
गन्ध बाड़े, तैछे एइ श्लोकेर विचार ॥192॥
cc-madhya-4.192.translation: By continuous rubbing, the aroma of Malaya sandalwood increases. Similarly, by considering this verse, its importance increases.

devanagari: रत्न - गण - मध्ये यैछे कौस्तुभ - मणि ।
रस - काव्य - मध्ये तैछे एइ श्लोक गणि ॥193॥
cc-madhya-4.193.translation: As the Kaustubha-maṇi is considered the most precious of valuable stones, this verse is similarly considered the best of mellow poems.

devanagari: एइ श्लोक कहियाछेन राधा - ठाकुराणी ।
ताँर कृपाय स्फुरियाछे माधवेन्द्र - वाणी ॥194॥
cc-madhya-4.194.translation: Actually this verse was spoken by Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī Herself, and by Her mercy only was it manifest in the words of Mādhavendra Purī.

devanagari: किबा गौरचन्द्र इहा करे आस्वादन ।
इहा आस्वादिते आर नाहि चौठ - जन ॥195॥
cc-madhya-4.195.translation: Only Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu has tasted the poetry of this verse. No fourth man is capable of understanding it.

devanagari: शेष - काले एइ श्लोक पठिते पठिते ।
सिद्धि - प्राप्ति हैल पुरीर श्लोकेर सहिते ॥196॥
cc-madhya-4.196.translation: Mādhavendra Purī recited this verse again and again at the end of his material existence. Thus uttering this verse, he attained the ultimate goal of life.

devanagari: अयि दीन - दयार्द्र नाथ हे मथुरा - नाथ कदावलोक्यसे ।
हृदयं त्वदलोक - कातरं दयित भ्राम्यति किं करोम्यहम् ॥197॥
cc-madhya-4.197.translation: "O My Lord! O most merciful master! O master of Mathurā! When shall I see You again? Because of My not seeing You, My agitated heart has become unsteady. O most beloved one, what shall I do now?"

lines: ei śloka paḍite prabhu ha-ilā mūrcchite
devanagari: एइ श्लोक पड़िते प्रभु हइला मूर्च्छिते ।
प्रेमेते विवश ह ञा पड़िल भूमिते ॥198॥
cc-madhya-4.198.translation: When Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu recited this verse, He immediately fell to the ground unconscious. He was overwhelmed and had no control over Himself.

devanagari: आस्ते - व्यस्ते कोले क रि’ निल नित्यानन्द ।
क्रन्दन करिया तबे उठे गौरचन्द्र ॥199॥
cc-madhya-4.199.translation: When Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu fell to the ground in ecstatic love, Lord Nityānanda took Him on His lap. Crying, Caitanya Mahāprabhu then got up again.

devanagari: जय जय गौरचन्द्र जय नित्यानन्द ।
जयाद्वैतचन्द्र जय गौर - भक्त - वृन्द ॥2॥
cc-madhya-4.2.translation: All glories to Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu! All glories to Advaita Prabhu! And all glories to all the devotees of Lord Caitanya!

lines: pūrve mādhava-purīra lāgi' kṣīra kaila curi
devanagari: पूर्वे माधव - पुरीर लागि’ क्षीर कैल चुरि ।
अतएव नाम हैल ‘क्षीर - चोरा ह रि’ ॥20॥
cc-madhya-4.20.translation: Formerly the Deity had stolen a pot of sweet rice for Mādhavendra Purī; therefore He became very famous as the Lord who stole the sweet rice.

lines: huṅkāra karaye, hāse, kānde, nāce, gāya
devanagari: प्रेमोन्माद हैल, उठि’ इति - उति धाय ।
हुङ्कार करये, हासे, कान्दे, नाचे, गाय ॥200॥
cc-madhya-4.200.translation: Exhibiting ecstatic emotions, the Lord began to run here and there, making resounding noises. Sometimes He laughed, and sometimes He cried, and sometimes He danced and sang.

lines: kaṇṭhe nā niḥsare vāṇī, netre aśru-dhāra
devanagari: ‘अयि दीन, ‘अयि दी न’ बले बार - बार ।
कण्ठे ना निःसरे वाणी, नेत्रे अश्रु - धार ॥201॥
cc-madhya-4.201.translation: Caitanya Mahāprabhu could not recite the whole verse. He simply said, "Ayi dīna, ayi dīna," repeatedly. Thus He could not speak, and profuse tears were in His eyes.

lines: nirveda, viṣāda, jāḍya, garva, harṣa, dainya
devanagari: कम्प, स्वेद, पुलकाश्रु, स्तम्भ, वैवर्ण्य ।
निर्वेद, विषाद, जाड्य, गर्व, हर्ष, दैन्य ॥202॥
cc-madhya-4.202.translation: Trembling, perspiration, jubilant tears, shock, fading of the bodily luster, disappointment, moroseness, loss of memory, pride, joy and humility were all visible in Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's body.

devanagari: एइ श्लोके उघाड़िला प्रेमेर कपाट ।
गोपीनाथ - सेवक देखे प्रभुर प्रेम - नाट ॥203॥
